A pink rubber band wrapped around a Soviet rifle stock wasn't decoration — it held a first aid kit in place. Soviet soldiers in Afghanistan used an Esmarch tourniquet, designed to stop catastrophic bleeding, as a strap to attach medical supplies directly to their weapon. It guaranteed that whatever happened in combat, they'd always have their first aid kit within reach on the one object they were guaranteed to still be holding. A simple, unofficial battlefield innovation with life-saving intent.
